steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on learning generalized structured weight matrices for efficient DNNs in a differentiable way. Motivate the problem with growing model sizes and hand-crafted structured matrices, pose our two research questions, and list our contributions (the GBLR format, the Gaudi parameterization, and the training algorithm).

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have been very successful in recent years in various domains, both for large language models (LLMs) and for vision tasks. But the size of DNNs has grown on an extraordinary scale, up to 70 Billion parameters in a single model, and deploying DNN-based services now needs an unprecedented amount of computing resources and energy. Fortunately, under certain conditions, the weight matrices of DNNs trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) naturally have well-defined preferred structures, such as low-rank matrices. However, it is still a challenging problem to identify such structures to lower the effective complexity of weight matrices in recent models such as Transformers. Also, it mostly depends on existing human-designed / hand-crafted structured matrices and there is no unified systematic approach. So prior works have focused on investigating new classes of structured matrices for DNNs. Each structured matrix is defined separately from the other formats. For example, a block-sparse matrix format and a low-rank matrix format with the same number of parameters are not subsets of each other, and still there is no unified representation that describes both well. Also, the structure description and the implementation complexity of the structured matrix are in non-differentiable discrete spaces.

In this paper, we investigate (locally) optimal structures of the weight matrices and also a differentiable training method to learn them, and we try to answer the following two questions:

- 1. Is there a universal format that represents a wide range of structured matrices?

- 2. Can the structure of such matrices be learned efficiently, if it exists?

- Contributions: generalized, differentiable structured matrix format
  - 1) Generalized Block-low-rank (GBLR): includes LR, BSP, BLR under practical conditions; structural params + content params; LR/BSP/BLR special cases; closed under interpolation in structural parameter space -> may capture undiscovered formats
  - 2) differentiable parameterization of structural params (widths, locations of blocks); defined in frequency domain; Gaussian-Dirichlet (Gaudi) function + inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) -> Gaudi-GBLR; derivatives exist almost everywhere, even width zero
  - 3) learning algorithm based on proximal gradient descent; evaluated on ViT (cite) and MLP-Mixer (cite); beats hand-designed structured matrices

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have been very successful in recent years in various domains, both for large language models (LLMs) and for vision tasks. But the size of DNNs has grown on an extraordinary scale, up to 70 Billion parameters in a single model, and deploying DNN-based services now needs an unprecedented amount of computing resources and energy. Fortunately, under certain conditions, the weight matrices of DNNs trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) naturally have well-defined preferred structures, such as low-rank matrices. However, it is still a challenging problem to identify such structures to lower the effective complexity of weight matrices in recent models such as Transformers. Also, it mostly depends on existing human-designed / hand-crafted structured matrices and there is no unified systematic approach. So prior works have focused on investigating new classes of structured matrices for DNNs. Each structured matrix is defined separately from the other formats. For example, a block-sparse matrix format and a low-rank matrix format with the same number of parameters are not subsets of each other, and still there is no unified representation that describes both well. Also, the structure description and the implementation complexity of the structured matrix are in non-differentiable discrete spaces.

In this paper, we investigate (locally) optimal structures of the weight matrices and also a differentiable training method to learn them, and we try to answer the following two questions:

- 1. Is there a universal format that represents a wide range of structured matrices?

- 2. Can the structure of such matrices be learned efficiently, if it exists?

Contributions. To tackle these two questions, we introduce a generalized and differentiable structured matrix format. The main contributions of this work are as follows.

1) We propose a Generalized Block-low-rank (GBLR) matrix format, which includes many important structures such as Low-Rank (LR), Block Sparse (BSP), and Block-low-rank (BLR) matrices under some practical conditions. The new format has two types of parameters: one guides the structure of the matrix and the other specifies the content or the values of matrix elements. We show that the LR, BSP and BLR formats are special cases of the GBLR matrix. We also show that the GBLR format is closed under interpolation between existing GBLR matrices in the structural parameter space, and we think this is strong evidence that the GBLR format can capture undiscovered structured matrix formats.

2) We introduce a differentiable parameterization of the structural parameters of the GBLR format, which are the widths and locations of blocks. The structural parameters are defined in the frequency domain, and they are processed by the proposed Gaussian-Dirichlet (Gaudi) function and then inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT), giving the format we call Gaudi-GBLR. We show that the derivatives of the Gaudi function with respect to the structural parameters exist almost everywhere, even when the width is zero.

3) We propose a practical learning algorithm based on proximal gradient descent to train compact neural networks with Gaudi-GBLR matrices. We evaluate the method extensively on Vision Transformers (ViT) and MLP-Mixer, and it outperforms prior approaches that use hand-designed structured matrices.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) for large language models (LLMs) [1,2,3,4] and vision tasks [5,6] have shown great success in various domains in recent years. The size of DNNs, however, has increased on an extraordinary scale, up to 70 Billion parameters in a single model [7], requiring an unprecedented amount of computing resources and energy to deploy DNN-based services. Fortunately, under certain conditions, the weight matrices of DNNs trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) naturally have well-defined preferred structures, such as low-rank matrices [8,9,10]. However, identifying such structures to lower the effective complexity of weight matrices in recent models such as Transformers [1] remains a challenging problem. It also mostly relies on existing human-designed / hand-crafted structured matrices without a unified systematic approach. Hence prior works have focused on investigating new classes of structured matrices for DNNs [11,12,13]. Notably, each structured matrix is defined separately from the other formats. For example, neither the block-sparse matrix format nor the low-rank matrix format with the same number of parameters is a subset of the other, and yet there is no unified representation that describes both well. Moreover, the structure description and the implementation complexity of the structured matrix lie in non-differentiable discrete spaces.

In this paper, we investigate (locally) optimal structures of the weight matrices as well as a differentiable training method to learn them, attempting to answer the following two questions:

- 1. Is there a universal format that represents a wide range of structured matrices?

- 2. Can the structure of such matrices be learned efficiently, if it exists?

Contributions. Tackling these two questions, we introduce a generalized and differentiable structured matrix format. The main contributions of this work can be summarized as follows.

1) We propose a Generalized Block-low-rank (GBLR) matrix format, which includes many important structures such as Low-Rank (LR), Block Sparse (BSP), and Block-low-rank (BLR) matrices under some practical conditions. The new structured matrix format consists of two types of parameters: one guiding the structure of the matrix and the other specifying the content or the values of matrix elements. We show that the LR, BSP and BLR formats are special cases of the GBLR matrix. We also show that the GBLR format is closed under interpolation between existing GBLR matrices in the structural parameter space, which we believe is strong evidence that the GBLR format is able to capture undiscovered structured matrix formats.

2) We introduce a differentiable parameterization of the structural parameters (widths and locations of blocks) of the GBLR format. The structural parameters are defined in the frequency domain and are processed by the proposed Gaussian-Dirichlet (Gaudi) function followed by inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT), giving the format named Gaudi-GBLR. We show that the derivatives of the Gaudi function with respect to the structural parameters exist almost everywhere, even when the width is zero.

3) We propose a practical learning algorithm based on proximal gradient descent to train compact neural networks with Gaudi-GBLR matrices. The proposed method is extensively evaluated on Vision Transformers (ViT) [5] and MLP-Mixer [14], outperforming prior approaches that use hand-designed structured matrices.
